name: Mont-Saint-Michel Island Abbey
builtBy: Bishop Aubert of Avranches and Capetian Kings
description: Gravity-defying Gothic Benedictine abbey perched atop a tidal granite island in Normandy, cut off from the mainland at high tide.
history: Major medieval Christian pilgrimage destination that withstood repeated English sieges during the Hundred Years' War.
construction: Constructed from granite transported across sand flats at low tide, engineered to follow the steep conical shape of the island rock.
architecture: Showcases 'La Merveille' (The Wonder)—a three-story masterpiece of Gothic architecture with a cloister suspended between sky and sea.
